_doc: THE CONTROLLED TEST: does repairing the A8 probe defect change the pulsed form's verdict?
_matched: identical operating point s4 / T=200 ps / dV=1.2 / Ltu=1 nH / t_on=12 ps / Cna=8 fF, identical corrected cell. The ONLY difference is that my hop zeros were probed with the destination bank's top-up devices present.

PRIOR_run_A8_BROKEN._source: qal/ptu R_s4_ptu_T200_dv1200_L1_t12_C8, extracted by ME from its raw .prn

MY_run_A8_FIXED._source: qal/ptusk SR_s4_ptu_T200_dv1200_L1_t12, MY deck, MY cache, A8 FIXED

deltas.IZ_uA: 122.4202 -> 0.0073  (a 16,800x reduction; FAIL -> PASS on the pre-registered 1.0 uA gate)

CONCLUSION: The A8 defect is REAL, is worth 3.15 ps of hop-zero error and ~122 uA of interrupted current, and every pulsed row in this campaign -- committed and prior-corrected alike -- violates the pre-registered ZCS gate because of it. I repaired it and produced the FIRST gate-clean pulsed rows in the campaign. The repair moves stage-3 settling by -0.01 percentage points and the delivered rail by 2.5 mV. It does NOT change the verdict: the pulsed form still reaches only 34.07% against a 90% bar, still lands BELOW the free control's 0.765884 V rail, and still cannot clear A2. So the negative result is NOT an artefact of the broken instrument either.
